items.title: The first Impressionist show
items.claim: What was the first Impressionist exhibition called?

options.text: Exposition of the Anonymous Society of Painters, Sculptors and Engravers

items.reveal:
The exhibition opened on 15 April 1874 in Nadar's former studio. The label 'Impressionists' came from a critic, Louis Leroy, mocking Monet's Impression, soleil levant.

The group held eight exhibitions between 1874 and 1886.
items.why: Movement names often come from hostile critics rather than the artists themselves.

items.title: Banksy's self-shredding
items.claim: In October 2018 a Banksy work partially shredded during a Sotheby's auction. What happened to the price after the stunt?

options.text: It sold for the auction price, then resold in 2021 for around £18.6 million
The buyer sued and won damages

items.reveal:
Originally hammered at around £1 million on 5 October 2018, the partially shredded work was renamed Love Is in the Bin and resold in October 2021 for around £18.6 million.

The shredder was concealed in the frame.
items.why: Critiques of art markets can become market assets themselves.

items.title: Kandinsky and abstraction
items.claim: Wassily Kandinsky's 1911 book Concerning the Spiritual in Art argued for non-representational painting drawing on what analogy?

options.text: Music as a purely formal art moving the soul

items.reveal:
Kandinsky argued colour and form could affect viewers directly, as harmony and rhythm do in music.

His Compositions and Improvisations are titled after musical genres.
items.why: Abstraction needed a theoretical framework before audiences could read it as art.
